definition: Interject means to insert a remark into a conversation.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word interject. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know interject should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Court reporters dread twins on the witness stand: each will interject a correction the instant the other rounds a number up.
A comment waits its turn and enters when the floor is free; it stops short of interject, which slides a remark into a live pause.
Interrupt goes further than a comment ever does — it cuts the speaker off mid-sentence and takes the floor, precisely the shove an interjection avoids.

To interpose is to place a remark — or yourself — between other speakers, stepping briefly into their exchange. It is stiffer and more formal than interject, at home in committee minutes and diplomatic notes, and it still defers to the speakers around it, as an interjection does.

To blurt is to let a remark burst out unplanned — the words escape before judgment catches them. To interject can be perfectly deliberate: the speaker waits for the right pause and places the remark exactly there. Blurting is an accident of timing; interjecting is timing used well.

A live broadcast control room runs on one unbreakable rule: the director's channel stays clear.
Producers, engineers, and statisticians all listen, but they interject only in the gaps -- a score correction dropped in while the director draws breath between camera calls.
Rookies get this wrong in both directions.
Some talk over a call and get muted; others wait so politely that their fact arrives thirty seconds after it mattered.
The best learn to read the rhythm.
A pause after 'take three' lasts half a second, and half a second is enough.
One veteran producer put it this way: the skill is not knowing what to say, which is easy, but hearing the exact silence that has room for it.
